transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

Samsung 4C means the washer isn’t detecting enough incoming water. If the drum remains completely dry, it is most likely a supply/connection issue rather than drainage.

Before booking a repair, try:

1. Check the water tap is fully open
• The washer normally uses the cold-water supply.
• Make sure the isolation valve behind/near the machine has not been knocked partly closed.

2. Check the inlet hose
• Ensure it isn’t kinked, crushed behind the machine, or twisted.
• Turn off the tap, unscrew the hose from the machine and briefly aim it into a bucket/tub (carefully turn the tap on) to confirm there is a strong flow from the plumbing.

3. Clean the small inlet filter
• With the tap off and hose removed from the machine, look inside the machine’s water inlet connection.
• There is usually a small mesh filter. Carefully pull it out with tweezers/pliers, rinse away limescale/debris, and refit it. Don’t run the machine without it.

4. Check for a blocked hose-end filter
• Some hoses have a gauze/filter in the hose fitting too. Inspect and rinse this as well.

5. Check the drain hose isn’t causing siphoning
• It should not be shoved too far down the standpipe, and the standpipe connection should not be sealed airtight.
• If water is entering briefly then immediately draining away, the machine can eventually report 4C. However, if the drum never gets wet at all, this is less likely.

6. Reset and test
• Switch the machine off at the wall for 5 minutes, then try a rinse cycle with no laundry.

If there is good water pressure at the disconnected hose, the tap is open, and the filters are clean, the likely fault is the machine’s water inlet valve (or less commonly its wiring/control board). That generally warrants an engineer rather than further DIY, especially as it involves opening the machine and working around mains/water connections.

Do not keep repeatedly starting it if you can hear it trying to fill but no water enters.

Tap was open (I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway, no change) and the hose isn't kinked. The mesh filter at the machine end was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. I cleaned it and refitted it, and now it fills normally and the 4C has gone.

Great — that would do it. The clogged inlet filter was restricting the water flow enough for the machine to time out and show 4C.

A couple of useful follow-ups:

• Run an empty rinse or short cycle once, just to flush through anything disturbed.
• Check the filter again in a few weeks; if it has collected more grit, your supply may be shedding debris/limescale.
• If you’re in a hard-water area, cleaning that inlet mesh periodically can prevent it recurring.
• Make sure the filter is seated properly and the hose connection is hand-tight, then check for drips during the next wash.

No call-out needed if it continues filling normally.
